context.body: Noah’s preservation is embedded inside an argument centered on Christ rather than retold for its own sake.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Christ’s suffering, death, life in the Spirit, proclamation to imprisoned spirits, divine patience, Noah’s ship, eight people, and water appear in one compressed sequence.
observations.label: Peter carries Noah’s water into a difficult baptism argument: action

observations.body: Baptism is called a corresponding figure and is distinguished from bodily dirt removal through conscience, resurrection, and Christ’s exaltation.
observations.label: Peter carries Noah’s water into a difficult baptism argument: response

observations.body: spirits in prison · days of Noah · saved through water · corresponding baptism
observations.label: Words in 1 Peter 3:18–22

payload.posture: Read 1 Peter 3:18–22 as warning, faith, and water evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The connections among proclamation, spirits, water, baptism, and Noah remain textually difficult and must not be over-harmonized.
payload.title: Peter carries Noah’s water into a difficult baptism argument
